subject: R/qtl marker/population size limits re: linkage mapping

messages.author: c21014a119b81c26
messages.subject: R/qtl marker/population size limits re: linkage mapping
parts:
Karl:  

I have been using R/qtl for genetic map construction for some time now, but do not know if there are marker number and population size limits in using R/qtl commands for this purpose.  

My colleagues and I have a soybean population of 1500 F5-derived RILs obtained from a biparental mating of homozygous parents (G. max x G. soja).  We would like to order about 2000 polymorphic SNP markers on each of the 20 soybean chromosomes, though we recognize that the extent of recombination available in this population will impose limits on marker ordering).  The soybean has a total (Kosambi) map length of about 2500 cM).  

The purpose of this project is to help us deal with a few assembly sequence problems in the published soybean DNA sequence.  

Can one use the R commands described in http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf to handle this many markers and individuals?  

We would welcome any suggestions you might offer with respect to computer specifications (memory, etc.) to handle this problem.  

Thanks in advance for your reply.  

- Jim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] R/qtl marker/population size limits re: linkage mapping
parts:
There's no limit on the number of markers or individuals that can be handled within R/qtl.  Analyses are slower, and some plots become hard to read, but 1500 RILs at 2000 SNPs shouldn't pose a problem.

karl
